verses.text: Joash was seven years old when he became king, and he ruled for forty years in Jerusalem. His mother was Zibiah from Beersheba.
Joash did what was right in the LORD's eyes for as long as Jehoiada the priest was alive.
Jehoiada chose two wives for him, and he had sons and daughters.
Some time later, Joash decided to repair the LORD's temple.

He called the priests and Levites together and said to them, "Go out to the towns of Judah and collect money from all Israel every year to repair the temple of your God. Do it quickly." But the Levites did not hurry.

So the king called for Jehoiada, the chief priest, and asked him, "Why haven't you made the Levites bring in the tax from Judah and Jerusalem? Moses, the LORD's servant, and the people of Israel set this tax for the Tent of the Covenant."
The sons of that wicked woman Athaliah had broken into God's temple and had used even the holy things of the LORD's temple for the Baal gods.
So at the king's order, they made a wooden box and put it outside, at the gate of the LORD's temple.
Then they announced all through Judah and Jerusalem that the people should bring to the LORD the tax that Moses, God's servant, had set for Israel in the desert.
All the leaders and all the people were happy to do it. They brought their money and dropped it into the box until it was full.

Whenever the Levites brought the box to the king's officials and they saw that there was a lot of money in it, the king's secretary and the chief priest's officer came and emptied it. Then they took the box back to its place. They did this day after day and collected a lot of money.

The king and Jehoiada gave the money to the men in charge of the work on the LORD's temple. They hired stoneworkers and carpenters to repair the LORD's temple, and workers in iron and bronze to fix it.
The workers worked hard, and the repairs went well. They rebuilt God's temple the way it was designed and made it strong.

When they had finished, they brought the money that was left to the king and Jehoiada. With it they made things for the LORD's temple: things for the temple service and for the offerings, including dishes and other objects of gold and silver. As long as Jehoiada lived, burnt offerings were offered in the LORD's temple all the time.
Jehoiada grew old and lived a long, full life. He died when he was one hundred thirty years old.
He was buried with the kings in the City of David, because he had done so much good in Israel for God and his temple.
After Jehoiada died, the leaders of Judah came and bowed down to the king, and the king listened to their advice.
They left the temple of the LORD, the God of their ancestors, and worshiped Asherah poles and idols. Because of this sin, God was angry with Judah and Jerusalem.
Still the LORD sent prophets to them to bring them back to him. The prophets warned them, but they would not listen.

Then the Spirit of God came on Zechariah, son of Jehoiada the priest. He stood up above the people and said to them, "God says: 'Why do you disobey the LORD's commands? You will not do well. Because you have left the LORD, he has left you.'"
But they plotted against him, and at the king's order they stoned him to death in the courtyard of the LORD's temple.
King Joash did not remember how kind Zechariah's father Jehoiada had been to him. Instead he killed his son. As Zechariah was dying, he said, "May the LORD see this and pay you back."
At the end of the year, the Syrian army came to attack Joash. They invaded Judah and Jerusalem, killed all the leaders of the people, and sent all the loot to their king in Damascus.
The Syrian army was only a small group of men, but the LORD handed a very large army over to them, because Judah had left the LORD, the God of their ancestors. In this way Joash was punished.

When the Syrians left, Joash was badly wounded. His own officials plotted against him because he had killed the son of Jehoiada the priest. They killed him in his bed, and he died. He was buried in the City of David, but not in the tombs of the kings.
The men who plotted against him were Zabad, son of Shimeath, a woman from Ammon, and Jehozabad, son of Shimrith, a woman from Moab.
The story of his sons, the many prophecies against him, and the rebuilding of God's temple are written in the notes on the book of the kings. His son Amaziah became king after him.
